question.prompt: A school has \(100\) students and \(5\) teachers. In the first period, each student is taking one class, and each teacher is teaching one class. The enrollments in the classes are \(50,\) \(20,\) \(20,\) \(5,\) and \(5.\) Let \(t\) be the average value obtained if a teacher is picked at random and the number of students in their class is noted. Let \(s\) be the average value obtained if a student was picked at random and the number of students in their class, including the student, is noted. What is \(t - s?\)

solutions.title: Weight classes by who is chosen
solutions.explanation:
Choosing a teacher gives each class the same chance of being selected. Choosing a student gives larger classes more weight, since they contain more students.

For the five equally likely teachers, the average class size is
\[
t=\frac{50+20+20+5+5}{5}=20.
\]
Of the \(100\) students, \(50\) are in the class of size \(50\), \(40\) are in classes of size \(20\), and \(10\) are in classes of size \(5\). Thus the student average is
\[
s=\frac{50}{100}\cdot50+\frac{40}{100}\cdot20+\frac{10}{100}\cdot5
=\frac{2500+800+50}{100}=33.5.
\]
Therefore
\[
t-s=20-33.5=\boxed{-13.5},
\]
which is choice \(\text{B}\).
